learningProfile.name: Rule-Based Mean Reversion
learningProfile.riskRules: Measure the educational invalidation distance in Gold points or dollars from the stretch area to the failed-expansion boundary.
learningProfile.whenToUse: Rule-Based Mean Reversion (GD-222 GOLD) Use the lesson when the mean line, deviation band, and close back toward the mean can all be marked before the classroom result is judged.
learningProfile.whyExists: Rule-Based Mean Reversion (GD-222 GOLD) It exists because Gold often stretches away from a short-term fair area, yet the stretch only matters when the learner can name the range, deviation band, and failure condition.
learningProfile.whyUseful: Rule-Based Mean Reversion (GD-222 GOLD) It trains discipline: the learner sees that a mean-reversion idea is a rule audit, not a reaction to any candle that looks extended.

setupLogic.action: GD-222 GOLD: mark the range and mean line first.
setupLogic.reason: The mean must be known before stretch is judged.

setupLogic.action: GD-222 GOLD: plot the deviation band and stretch candle.
setupLogic.reason: The learner sees why price is considered extended.

setupLogic.action: GD-222 GOLD: wait for a close back toward the mean.
setupLogic.reason: A wick alone is not enough.

setupLogic.action: GD-222 GOLD: label the failed-expansion boundary.
setupLogic.reason: The setup needs a clear wrong point.

learningProfile.commonTraps: Rule-Based Mean Reversion (GD-222 GOLD) trap: The main trap is calling every large candle a stretch even when Gold is beginning a new expansion leg.
learningProfile.targetLogic: Use the mean line and the opposite side of the range as educational reference zones, not as promises.
learningProfile.setupContext: Rule-Based Mean Reversion (GD-222 GOLD) Use it when Gold is moving inside a readable range, deviation from the mean is visible, and the wick behavior shows rejection instead of clean expansion.
learningProfile.whenNotToUse: Rule-Based Mean Reversion (GD-222 GOLD) Skip it when Gold is expanding through the band with strong closes or when macro news has made the old mean unreliable.
learningProfile.suitableMarkets: Gold examples should use XAU movement with visible range structure, wick reaction, and point/dollar distance from stretch to invalidation.
learningProfile.tradeManagement: Keep checking whether price is still returning toward the mean or has changed into accepted expansion.
learningProfile.beginnerMistakes: Rule-Based Mean Reversion (GD-222 GOLD) learner mistakes: Learner mistakes include moving the mean after the fact, ignoring the failed-expansion boundary, and using one wick without a close.
learningProfile.suitableSessions: Use active Gold windows where wick behavior and event volatility can be compared clearly.
learningProfile.confirmationRules: Confirmation is a completed close back inside the deviation band plus price respecting the mean-reversion path.
learningProfile.invalidationRules: The idea is invalidated when Gold closes beyond the deviation band and accepts expansion instead of returning toward the mean.

learningProfile.whyExists: Volatility-Targeted System (GD-223 GOLD) It exists because the same chart idea can become too large when Gold volatility rises, even if the direction read still looks clean.
learningProfile.whyUseful: Volatility-Targeted System (GD-223 GOLD) It connects volatility, size, and drawdown control in plain terms so the learner can see why exposure changes before stress builds.

learningProfile.whyExists: Regime-Switching Model (GD-224 GOLD) It exists because Gold can shift between trend, range, macro shock, and quiet conditions, and each state needs different handling.
learningProfile.whyUseful: Regime-Switching Model (GD-224 GOLD) It helps the learner pause when evidence is mixed instead of forcing one rule onto every market state.

learningProfile.name: ATR-Based Position Sizing
learningProfile.riskRules: Use a fixed educational risk budget and Gold point/dollar distance to calculate the classroom size.
learningProfile.whenToUse: ATR-Based Position Sizing (GD-232 GOLD) Use the lesson when ATR distance and structure distance can both be measured before size is calculated.
learningProfile.whyExists: ATR-Based Position Sizing (GD-232 GOLD) It exists because Gold movement changes over time, and a fixed size can become too large when ATR expands.
learningProfile.whyUseful: ATR-Based Position Sizing (GD-232 GOLD) It makes size visible as a calculation rather than a feeling.

setupLogic.action: GD-232 GOLD: record current ATR.
setupLogic.reason: Movement size comes first.

setupLogic.action: GD-232 GOLD: measure structure invalidation distance.
setupLogic.reason: Distance controls sizing.

setupLogic.action: GD-232 GOLD: apply the classroom risk budget.
setupLogic.reason: The size is calculated.

setupLogic.action: GD-232 GOLD: label volatility-spike caution.
setupLogic.reason: One candle can distort ATR.

learningProfile.commonTraps: ATR-Based Position Sizing (GD-232 GOLD) trap: The trap is using ATR as a direction clue instead of a movement-size input.
learningProfile.targetLogic: Use the sizing panel and invalidation distance as the educational reference.
learningProfile.setupContext: ATR-Based Position Sizing (GD-232 GOLD) Use it when ATR is current, the invalidation line is clear, and the classroom risk budget is written.
learningProfile.whenNotToUse: ATR-Based Position Sizing (GD-232 GOLD) Skip it when ATR is distorted by one news candle or the invalidation area is unclear.
learningProfile.suitableMarkets: Gold examples should include current ATR, XAU structure, and point/dollar distance.
learningProfile.tradeManagement: Recalculate size when ATR changes materially or when the invalidation line moves.
learningProfile.beginnerMistakes: ATR-Based Position Sizing (GD-232 GOLD) learner mistakes: Learner mistakes include using stale ATR, ignoring the structure line, and rounding size upward without a reason.

learningProfile.confirmationRules: Confirmation is a size calculation that changes when ATR or invalidation distance changes.
learningProfile.invalidationRules: The sizing lesson is invalidated when size is chosen before distance and risk budget are known.

learningProfile.name: Leverage Control
learningProfile.riskRules: Use point/dollar distance and a fixed buffer to show when exposure must be reduced.
learningProfile.whenToUse: Leverage Control (GD-233 GOLD) Use the lesson when the leverage cap and cutback rule can be applied before judging the chart idea.
learningProfile.whyExists: Leverage Control (GD-233 GOLD) It exists because leverage can make normal Gold movement feel extreme, especially when spreads or volatility widen.
learningProfile.whyUseful: Leverage Control (GD-233 GOLD) It helps the learner see leverage as a risk dial with a cap, buffer, and cutback rule.

setupLogic.action: GD-233 GOLD: write the leverage cap.
setupLogic.reason: The limit must be visible.

setupLogic.reason: Buffer protects the process.

setupLogic.action: GD-233 GOLD: apply exposure reduction gate.
setupLogic.reason: Cutback happens before stress.

learningProfile.targetLogic: Use the cap line, margin buffer, and cutback area as educational references.
learningProfile.setupContext: Leverage Control (GD-233 GOLD) Use it when leverage, margin buffer, volatility state, and point/dollar distance are visible.
learningProfile.whenNotToUse: Leverage Control (GD-233 GOLD) Skip it when the learner cannot explain the margin buffer or when event volatility makes the example unstable.
learningProfile.suitableMarkets: Gold examples should include XAU movement, volatility state, margin buffer, and point/dollar distance.
learningProfile.tradeManagement: Review leverage after volatility expands and pause the example if the buffer becomes too thin.

learningProfile.name: News Event Risk Reduction
learningProfile.riskRules: Use a reduced exposure rule or no-action window and measure Gold point/dollar movement after the event.
learningProfile.whenToUse: News Event Risk Reduction (GD-234 GOLD) Use the lesson before a scheduled event when Gold exposure can be reviewed calmly.
learningProfile.whyExists: News Event Risk Reduction (GD-234 GOLD) It exists because Gold can wick sharply around data releases, central-bank comments, and macro surprises.
learningProfile.whyUseful: News Event Risk Reduction (GD-234 GOLD) It turns news handling into a prewritten risk process instead of an emotional reaction during the event.

setupLogic.action: GD-234 GOLD: mark the event time and expected impact.
setupLogic.reason: Risk starts before the release.

setupLogic.action: GD-234 GOLD: draw the no-action window.
setupLogic.reason: Chaotic candles need separation.

setupLogic.action: GD-234 GOLD: review exposure reduction rule.
setupLogic.reason: Process comes before emotion.

setupLogic.action: GD-234 GOLD: label whipsaw trap.
setupLogic.reason: Gold can spike both ways.

learningProfile.commonTraps: News Event Risk Reduction (GD-234 GOLD) trap: The trap is reacting to the first news wick before the market shows stable acceptance.
learningProfile.targetLogic: Use the event window, pre-event range, and post-event stabilization area as educational references.
learningProfile.setupContext: News Event Risk Reduction (GD-234 GOLD) Use it when the event time, expected impact, spread/volatility state, and no-action window are visible.
learningProfile.whenNotToUse: News Event Risk Reduction (GD-234 GOLD) Skip active interpretation during the first chaotic release candles.
learningProfile.suitableMarkets: Gold examples should include event timing, XAU wick behavior, volatility expansion, and point/dollar distance.
learningProfile.tradeManagement: Do not judge the setup until spread and candle behavior normalize after the event.
learningProfile.beginnerMistakes: News Event Risk Reduction (GD-234 GOLD) learner mistakes: Learner mistakes include ignoring the calendar, studying a setup inside the no-action window, and forgetting spread expansion.
learningProfile.suitableSessions: Use Gold event windows with the pre-event and post-event candles clearly separated.
learningProfile.confirmationRules: Confirmation is the risk-reduction rule being applied before the event, not after the wick appears.
learningProfile.invalidationRules: The process fails when exposure is left unchanged despite a written high-impact event warning.

learningProfile.commonTraps: Previous-Day High Breakout (GD-238 GOLD) trap: The trap is treating a wick above yesterday's high as accepted breakout before the candle closes.

learningProfile.name: Structural Breakout (Retest)
learningProfile.riskRules: Measure pip distance from the retest area to the invalidation back inside the old range.
learningProfile.whenToUse: Structural Breakout (Retest) (FX-601 FOREX) Use the lesson when price closes beyond the level and returns to test it without falling back inside the old range.
learningProfile.whyExists: Structural Breakout (Retest) (FX-601 FOREX) It exists because many breaks fail when price returns into the old range, so the retest teaches acceptance versus rejection.
learningProfile.whyUseful: Structural Breakout (Retest) (FX-601 FOREX) It gives the learner a clean Level 2 structure lesson with a level, breakout close, retest, invalidation, spread, and pip distance.

setupLogic.action: FX-601 FOREX: mark the support/resistance level before the break.

setupLogic.action: FX-601 FOREX: study the retest on the new side.
setupLogic.reason: Acceptance is visible at the retest.

setupLogic.action: FX-601 FOREX: label old-range return trap.
setupLogic.reason: Failed breaks close back inside.

learningProfile.commonTraps: Structural Breakout (Retest) (FX-601 FOREX) trap: The trap is treating the first break as accepted when the retest immediately fails.
learningProfile.targetLogic: Use the next structure level on the new side of the break as the educational reference zone.
learningProfile.setupContext: Structural Breakout (Retest) (FX-601 FOREX) Use it when a Forex pair has a clear horizontal level, readable candles, normal spread, and room to the next structure.
learningProfile.whenNotToUse: Structural Breakout (Retest) (FX-601 FOREX) Skip it when the level is messy, spread is abnormal, or price breaks and immediately returns inside the range.
learningProfile.suitableMarkets: Forex examples should use a liquid pair with clear support/resistance, normal spread, and visible pip distance.
learningProfile.tradeManagement: Keep the level fixed and judge whether retest behavior shows acceptance or a failed return.

learningProfile.invalidationRules: The setup is invalidated when price closes back inside the old range after the retest.

learningProfile.name: Supertrend Volatility Stop
learningProfile.riskRules: Use pip distance from price to the band as an educational trailing invalidation measurement.
learningProfile.whenToUse: Use the lesson when band direction, completed pullback hold, spread, and pip distance can be marked.
learningProfile.whyExists: It exists because a Supertrend band can show where trend structure would be challenged after volatility is included.
learningProfile.whyUseful: It helps learners understand why trailing invalidation must adjust when Forex volatility expands or contracts.

setupLogic.action: mark the Supertrend volatility band
setupLogic.reason: The trailing line must be visible.

setupLogic.action: check trend structure and pullback quality
setupLogic.reason: Band read needs price context.

setupLogic.action: wait for completed hold or flip
setupLogic.reason: Unfinished candles can cross back.

setupLogic.action: record spread and pip distance
setupLogic.reason: Forex scale and cost matter.

learningProfile.commonTraps: The trap is reacting to every band flip in a choppy pair without checking structure and spread.
learningProfile.targetLogic: The educational reference is the structure area that price approaches while the band trails behind it.
learningProfile.setupContext: Use it when a Forex pair is trending, the Supertrend band is visible, and price is respecting pullbacks without repeated flips.
learningProfile.whenNotToUse: Skip it when price flips across the band repeatedly or the session spread distorts the stop distance.
learningProfile.learnerMistakes: Learner mistakes include treating the band as a forecast, ignoring pip distance, and skipping session spread.
learningProfile.suitableMarkets: Major Forex pairs with stable spread and visible Supertrend volatility band behavior.
learningProfile.tradeManagement: Keep the trailing line updated and label any flip-whipsaw before trusting the next read.
learningProfile.suitableSessions: London or New York windows where trend movement and spread can be compared.
learningProfile.confirmationRules: Confirmation is price holding the band after a completed pullback while the band direction stays intact.
learningProfile.invalidationRules: The read is invalidated when price closes through the band and the Supertrend flips.

learningProfile.name: Ichimoku Cloud Logic
learningProfile.riskRules: Use pip distance from the cloud boundary to the invalidation close as the classroom measurement.
learningProfile.whenToUse: Use the lesson when price location, cloud boundary, Tenkan/Kijun relationship, spread, and pip distance are visible.
learningProfile.whyExists: It exists because the cloud can organize trend and support/resistance context, but price location alone is incomplete.
learningProfile.whyUseful: It helps learners avoid reducing Ichimoku to one colored cloud by requiring line relationship, cloud thickness, and completed close.

setupLogic.action: mark cloud boundary and thickness
setupLogic.reason: The learner sees whether the cloud is readable.

setupLogic.action: compare Tenkan and Kijun relationship
setupLogic.reason: Line agreement gives context.

setupLogic.action: wait for completed close outside the cloud
setupLogic.reason: Wicks are not enough.

setupLogic.action: record spread and pip distance
setupLogic.reason: Forex scale stays explicit.

learningProfile.commonTraps: The trap is reading a cloud break while price is still inside a thick, indecisive cloud.
learningProfile.targetLogic: The educational reference is the next structure zone beyond the cloud after the close is accepted.
learningProfile.setupContext: Use it when a Forex pair has readable cloud structure, clear Tenkan/Kijun relationship, and normal session spread.
learningProfile.whenNotToUse: Skip it when price is inside a thick cloud or Tenkan and Kijun disagree without clear structure.
learningProfile.learnerMistakes: Learner mistakes include ignoring Tenkan/Kijun, skipping Chikou context, and using a wick instead of a close.
learningProfile.suitableMarkets: Major Forex pairs with clear Ichimoku cloud boundaries and stable spread.
learningProfile.tradeManagement: Keep checking cloud thickness and line relationship before judging the next candle.
learningProfile.suitableSessions: London or New York windows where completed closes around the cloud can be observed.
learningProfile.confirmationRules: Confirmation is a completed close outside the cloud with Tenkan/Kijun relationship supporting the structure.
learningProfile.invalidationRules: The read is invalidated when price closes back inside the cloud or the line relationship turns conflicted.

learningProfile.name: London Session Momentum
learningProfile.riskRules: Use pip distance from the expansion close to the failed return inside the range as the classroom invalidation measure.
learningProfile.whenToUse: Use the lesson when range boundary, London timing, stable close, spread, pullback or hold, and pip distance can all be marked.
learningProfile.whyExists: It exists because London can expand from the prior range, but the first move often includes spread widening and false starts.
learningProfile.whyUseful: It helps learners organize session timing, range boundary, stable close, pullback, and pip distance in one clean lesson.

setupLogic.action: mark the pre-London range before the open
setupLogic.reason: The boundary must be fixed in advance.

setupLogic.action: wait for the first stable London close
setupLogic.reason: The first fast candle can reverse.

setupLogic.action: check spread and pip distance
setupLogic.reason: Session cost and scale matter.

setupLogic.action: label pullback hold or false start
setupLogic.reason: Momentum needs acceptance.

learningProfile.commonTraps: The trap is chasing the first London candle while spread is wide and price has not closed outside the range.
learningProfile.targetLogic: The educational reference is the next London structure area after the range break and hold are visible.
learningProfile.setupContext: Use it when the pre-London range is clear and London expansion produces a completed close outside that range.
learningProfile.whenNotToUse: Skip it when the range is messy, spread widens sharply, or the first expansion candle closes back inside the range.
learningProfile.learnerMistakes: Learner mistakes include drawing the range after the break, ignoring spread widening, and judging momentum before the close.
learningProfile.suitableMarkets: Major Forex pairs that are active during London and show clear pre-session range structure.
learningProfile.tradeManagement: Track whether the first expansion holds or turns into a false start before judging continuation.
learningProfile.suitableSessions: Late Asia into London open, then the first stable London review window.
learningProfile.confirmationRules: Confirmation is a completed London close outside the pre-London range followed by a hold or controlled pullback.
learningProfile.invalidationRules: The read is invalidated when price closes back inside the pre-London range after the expansion.

practiceChecklist.item: pre-London range is fixed
practiceChecklist.reason: The level is not moved after the break.

learningProfile.suitableTimeframes: 5m, 15m, or 1H charts with the pre-London range and expansion candle visible.
learningProfile.sandboxInstructions: Mark pre-London high/low, London open, first stable close, pullback or hold, false-start trap, spread, and pip distance.
learningProfile.prerequisiteKnowledge: The learner should understand range high/low, London open timing, completed close, spread, and pip distance.
